It is increased prices and notes of improved industry discipline. Refers to winners (thos raising prices?) and losers (those not?).  "With the ongoing backdrop and demonstrably improved discipline within the rental industry, it is warranted and logical that we are increasing rental rates ... What we're seeing is winners and we are seeing losers. And ourselves and a couple of others out there are the real winners in that."

We're also seeing increased evidence of price discipline. ... 'We will continue our disciplined approach to decision making as we work to restore AIG as an industry leader. ... We have maintained our expected rate increases throughout the year, showing broad acceptance in the market."

Emphasizes that firms should invest in brands and not in aggressive pricing - firms which "solely reliant on discounting to continue to struggle" - and that competitors follow its prices: "as soon as we move price, the market tends to follow."  The latter is an observation rather than a suggestion.
Emphasizes that firms need to raise prices: ""...the industry has learned painfully that the way to actually grow EBITDA margins is to get the fleet right to demand and raise prices..."

If say, you have to put a number on it, I think the industry could operate with 30% or 35% less capacity than exists today."

Refers to constraining capacity and that more needs to be done: "we have been producing at higher levels than that, but then bear in mind that we are squeezing out a lot of capacity with overtime shifts. ...some of our other major competitors have publicly spoken about capacity constraints. ...there is a long way to go still and a big opportunity."
